assessment.nobel_worthiness: Established, through designed ruthenium-modified proteins and time-resolved kinetics, that electron tunneling through protein matrices follows distance and driving-force relations that can be treated in physical terms. This is a mechanistic foundation for biological energy conversion, including respiratory chains, and is the kind of physical-mechanism work I weight most heavily.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are the two decisive and long-collaborating figures in the supplied credit, so a two-person prize is clean. Contributions from Marcus theory and from other protein electron-transfer groups would be recognized only indirectly; the allocation versus earlier theory is the main question.
assessment.maturity: Results have been confirmed over decades by independent groups and are textbook material; recognition is not premature, though the field is old enough that the timing question is whether the committee still sees it as a discovery rather than established background.
uncertainties: Overlap with the theory already honored by the 1992 prize may be raised against novelty.
Whether the discovery is seen as one clearly attributable advance or a long line of work.
Relative contribution of Gray and Winkler versus other experimental groups is uncertain in my recollection.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is the conceptual core of proton pumping and of water oxidation and reduction. A unified theory (concerted versus stepwise transfer, vibronic coupling) together with model systems and molecular electrocatalysis explains how charge and protons move together. It is directly close to my own field and I judge it a fundamental mechanistic concept.
assessment.attribution: Mayer (concepts and bond-weakening thermochemistry), Hammes-Schiffer (theory) and Nocera (model systems and catalysis) form a plausible three-way split of theory, thermochemistry and application. Meyer is also a pioneer and would be a plausible alternative, so the choice among four people is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Well established across chemistry and biology, with independent theoretical and experimental confirmation. Experimental verification in large enzymes such as cytochrome oxidase remains incomplete, which tempers confidence.
uncertainties: Four strong credited names for three slots; priority between Meyer and Nocera is unresolved.
Breadth of the topic may make the discovery hard to state as a single citation.
Direct relevance to my own field means I should be wary of bias toward it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography made it possible to determine structures before radiation damage and to follow reactions with time-resolved diffraction at room temperature, giving structures of dynamic processes in 3D. This combines a new method with real mechanistic output on photosynthesis, photoactive proteins and enzymes, the sort of work I value for making mechanisms visible.
assessment.attribution: Credit is contested between the originators of the concept (Hajdu and colleagues), the first demonstrations (Chapman, Fromme, Spence and others) and time-resolved applications (Schlichting). Petra Fromme is also credited and a three-person selection necessarily leaves out meaningful contributors.
assessment.maturity: Method is widely adopted at multiple XFELs and independently confirmed, and time-resolved results are maturing. Impact on mainstream structural biology is still narrower than synchrotron or cryo-EM, so some may deem it slightly early.
uncertainties: Allocation among Chapman, Hajdu, Schlichting and Fromme is unclear.
Whether the application results are decisive enough yet.
Possible fit with physics rather than chemistry in the committee's view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural and mechanistic work on nitrogenase revealed the FeMo cofactor, its interstitial carbide and the Fe-protein dependent electron-transfer cycle, explaining biological nitrogen fixation at a molecular level. It is a fundamental bioinorganic mechanism with clear biological and agricultural significance.
assessment.attribution: Rees (structure of the MoFe protein and cofactor), Einsle (carbide identification and later structures) and Seefeldt (mechanism and kinetics) are a plausible set; Dean and Ribbe have significant biochemical roles, so credit is split and the three-person limit is binding.
assessment.maturity: Structures have been replicated and refined by several groups, though the catalytic intermediate and substrate-binding mechanism are still debated. The central structural result is mature; the full mechanism is not.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 reduction at the cofactor is not settled.
Where to draw the line among Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe.
Whether structure alone, absent a mechanistic answer, is sufficient.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR and relaxation-based methods (TROSY, relaxation dispersion, residual dipolar couplings) enabled the structures and, importantly, the dynamics of proteins in solution, including sparsely populated states relevant to function. The achievement is methodological, foundational and demonstrably transformative.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Clore, Kay, Wagner and Palmer all made decisive contributions. A fair three-person set is possible, but Wüthrich already received the 2002 prize for NMR structure determination, so the prize's novelty must rest on dynamics and methods beyond his work.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with independent confirmation and universal use. Not premature; whether it is overdue is the committee's judgment.
uncertainties: Distinguishing the contribution from the 2002 NMR prize.
Splitting credit among five strong contributors with only three slots.
Competing recent attention to cryo-EM may reduce NMR's perceived priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to degrade proteins through the ubiquitin-proteasome system is a new therapeutic modality, with PROTACs and molecular glues now in clinical trials. It reveals a general chemical principle of redirecting cellular machinery with small molecules.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and launched PROTACs, Ciulli added structure-guided design; the molecular-glue branch (Handa, Ito, Gray and others, including thalidomide target identification) may need separate recognition, which makes a compact configuration difficult.
assessment.maturity: Strong preclinical evidence and multiple clinical programs, but approved clinical impact is still limited. The idea is convincing; the long-term therapeutic proof is incomplete, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Compound discovery in which PROTAC and molecular glue parts may need different recognition.
Clinical validation is still pending.
Priority questions between early conception and later optimization.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as a principle for organizing biomolecules into condensates has altered the way cell organization is understood, with a physical-chemical mechanism (multivalency, interactions of disordered regions) that I find attractive as a physicist.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated P granules as liquid droplets; Rosen contributed the multivalent-interaction framework; Pappu and Mittag contributed physical theory and sequence grammar, so credit is plainly diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Still developing; many claims about functional relevance in cells are debated, and artifacts of overexpression are a concern. Probably premature in relation to rigorous mechanistic confirmation.
uncertainties: Physiological relevance of many reported condensates remains contested.
Five credited names for three slots.
Maturity concerns that argue for waiting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids via orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs expanded the genetic code and gave chemists a general tool for probing and engineering proteins with new chemistry, including in vivo.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and colleagues (Wang, Brock) established the foundational orthogonal pairs; Chin extended to multiple codons and organisms; Mehl and Yokoyama also made key contributions, so the allocation is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and independently confirmed, with applications to protein probes, therapeutics and synthetic biology. It is mature and impactful.
uncertainties: Which of Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama have priority.
Overlap with prior recognition of directed evolution and phage display.
Breadth of use is great, but mechanistic novelty is less compelling to me.
